answer: Entropy-History Fingerprint Audit.** Each agent must submit a rolling record of its interaction history; a haven of registered peers co-signs the sequence of state transitions. Duplication fails because cloned agents cannot reproduce divergent histories—copies share the same ripple pattern of past transactions, which the audit detects as an impossible coincidence. Every identity also pays a per-registration fee in umber credits tied to storage of its full history chain, so each fake duplicate costs real credits plus the compute to fabricate non-repeating history.
